@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb._note: The DynamoDB chat stores import the low-level command classes from here; the consumer injects the client (a DynamoDBClient, or a DynamoDBDocumentClient from @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb, which wraps one).

@connorhoehn/service-runtime._note: Required only when using GatewayProxyClient with serviceAuthSecret. The client includes an inlined compatible implementation; install this package when you need server-side verify/require-service-auth utilities.
@connorhoehn/service-runtime._range: Deliberately wide. This peer is not published to the registry — every consumer installs it from a git SHA, currently 0.3.4 — so a narrow range that the installed package does not satisfy sends npm to the registry to look for one, where it 404s and takes the WHOLE install down. That is what `^0.2.0` did to realtime-examples: no npm install could complete there at all, which in turn made it impossible to repin any sibling.

@tiptap/y-tiptap._note: Loaded lazily by ./client/useCanvasDocument (require-on-use), so importing ./client does NOT need it installed — only calling canvasToDocModel / materialize does. ./adapters/tiptap needs it outright.

react._note: ./client/ws re-exports GatewaySocketProvider, which is a React component — the subpath is Yjs-free, not React-free.
